lead: `nvs run --request` is not an HTML response, so `Core\Html::later` runs its closure at once there, with no `deadline`, no `error` fragment and no concurrency.
body: Under `--request`, `echo` writes plain text (an echoed `"<b>"` is not escaped), so `later` takes the path its card describes as "outside an HTML response", and an example blessed that way shows output the browser never gets. An example, an attack or a bench of `later` or a slotted response sends a real request with `Core\Test::request` instead, whose run assembles slots under the scheduler: `docs/examples/core/Html/later/01-two-parts-of-a-page.nvs` is the shape.
